record.original_question: Let A be a P-matrix, meaning that every principal minor A[α] is positive. Call A weakly sign-symmetric when A[α,β]A[β,α] ≥ 0 for every almost principal minor, i.e. for every minor whose dispersal #α − #(α ∩ β) equals 1. Such weakly sign-symmetric P-matrices are called GKK matrices. Call A a strict GKK matrix when the inequalities A[α,β]A[β,α] > 0 hold for all almost principal minors. Let l(A) be the smallest real eigenvalue of A, with l(A)=∞ if A has no real eigenvalues. A matrix is a τ-matrix when it has eigenvalue monotonicity l(A(α,α)) ≤ l(A(β,β)) < ∞ whenever ∅ ≠ β ⊆ α, and in addition l(A) ≥ 0. Which GKK matrices can be approximated arbitrarily well by strict GKK matrices, and in particular can the unstable matrices constructed in Holtz [11] be approximated by τ-matrices that are strict GKK?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $\langle n\rangle = \{1,\dots,n\}$. For a complex $n\times n$ matrix $A$ and index sets $\alpha,\beta\subseteq\langle n\rangle$ with $|\alpha|=|\beta|$, write $A[\alpha,\beta]$ for the minor of $A$ with row indices $\alpha$ and column indices $\beta$, and $A[\alpha]:=A[\alpha,\alpha]$ for the corresponding principal minor. The minor $A[\alpha,\beta]$ is called almost principal when its dispersal $|\alpha|-|\alpha\cap\beta|$ equals $1$. For $\alpha\subseteq\langle n\rangle$, let $A(\alpha,\alpha)$ denote the principal submatrix of $A$ on rows and columns indexed by $\alpha$.

Define:
(i) $A$ is a $P$-matrix if $A[\alpha]>0$ for every nonempty $\alpha\subseteq\langle n\rangle$.
(ii) $A$ is weakly sign-symmetric if $A[\alpha,\beta]\,A[\beta,\alpha]\ge 0$ for every almost principal minor; a weakly sign-symmetric $P$-matrix is called a GKK matrix.
(iii) $A$ is a strict GKK matrix if it is a $P$-matrix and $A[\alpha,\beta]\,A[\beta,\alpha]>0$ for every almost principal minor.
(iv) Let $\ell(A)$ denote the smallest real eigenvalue of $A$, with $\ell(A)=+\infty$ if $A$ has no real eigenvalue. Then $A$ is a $\tau$-matrix if $\ell(A(\alpha,\alpha))\le \ell(A(\beta,\beta))<\infty$ whenever $\emptyset\neq\beta\subseteq\alpha\subseteq\langle n\rangle$, and additionally $\ell(A)\ge 0$.

Characterize precisely which GKK matrices lie in the closure of the set of strict GKK matrices (with respect to the standard topology on $n\times n$ real or complex matrices). In particular, decide whether every unstable GKK $\tau$-matrix of the known constructed family (the $n\times n$ examples $A_{n,k,t}$ exhibiting GKK $\tau$-matrices that are not positively stable) can be approximated arbitrarily well in this topology by matrices that are simultaneously $\tau$-matrices and strict GKK.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is one of the open problems posed by Holtz and Schneider (2002) on GKK τ-matrices. A subsequent survey of structured-matrix problems by Holtz and Schneider (2005) reiterates these problems without resolution, and no later publication appears to characterize the closure of strict GKK matrices or prove approximability of the known unstable examples by strict GKK τ-matrices. Status appears to remain open.
